title: The Tunny-Fish and the Dolphin
attribution: Excerpted verbatim from Aesop's Fables, translated by V. S. Vernon Jones (1912), via Project Gutenberg.
body: A Tunny-fish was chased by a Dolphin and splashed through the water at a great rate, but the Dolphin gradually gained upon him, and was just about to seize him when the force of his flight carried the Tunny on to a sandbank. In the heat of the chase the Dolphin followed him, and there they both lay out of the water, gasping for dear life. When the Tunny saw that his enemy was doomed like himself, he said, "I don't mind having to die now: for I see that he who is the cause of my death is about to share the same fate."

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what was chasing the Tunny-fish?
options: A shark
A Dolphin
A fisherman's net
A larger tunny

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what happened as the Dolphin gained on the Tunny?
options: The Tunny turned to fight back
The force of the Tunny's flight carried him onto a sandbank
The Tunny dove to the bottom of the sea
The Dolphin lost interest and swam away

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what did the Dolphin do in the heat of the chase?
options: He stopped just short of the sandbank
He followed the Tunny onto the sandbank
He called out a warning to the Tunny
He swam around the sandbank instead

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what state were both fish in once out of the water?
options: Fighting each other fiercely
Gasping for dear life
Sleeping peacefully
Swimming in circles

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Tunny say he does not mind now?
options: Being caught by a fisherman
Having to die now
Losing the race
Being left on the sandbank alone

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "doomed" mean in "his enemy was doomed like himself"?
options: Certain to suffer the same fate, especially death
Guaranteed to escape safely
Completely unaware of danger
Free of any harm

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why is the Tunny able to find some comfort in his own death?
options: He believes he can still escape at the last moment
The very pursuit that caused his doom has also trapped and doomed his pursuer
He knows the Dolphin will be punished later by other dolphins
He expects a fisherman to rescue him before he dies

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the point of the fable?
options: It can be a grim consolation to see one's downfall shared by the one who caused it
Fish should never swim near sandbanks
Dolphins are always faster than tunny-fish
Chasing prey too eagerly always ends in success

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how did the Tunny-fish move through the water at first?
options: Slowly and cautiously
At a great rate
In wide, lazy circles
Along the sandy bottom

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what was the Dolphin just about to do when the Tunny reached the sandbank?
options: Turn back and give up
Seize him
Call for help from other dolphins
Dive beneath him

questions.prompt: According to the passage, where did both the Tunny and the Dolphin end up lying?
options: In a deep underwater cave
Out of the water, on the sandbank
Beneath a fisherman's boat
Tangled in seaweed

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "gained upon" mean in "the Dolphin gradually gained upon him"?
options: Lost ground to
Got closer to catching up with
Became afraid of
Swam away from

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what caused the Dolphin to end up stranded alongside the Tunny?
options: He was struck by a fisherman's spear
His own eagerness in the chase carried him onto the sandbank after his prey
He was too exhausted to swim back to deep water
He deliberately beached himself to catch the Tunny more easily

questions.prompt: Which of these best summarizes what happens in the passage?
options: A Dolphin chases a Tunny onto a sandbank where both become stranded, and the Tunny takes grim comfort in the Dolphin sharing his fate
A Tunny escapes a Dolphin by swimming into deep water
A Dolphin rescues a stranded Tunny from a sandbank
A fisherman catches both the Tunny and the Dolphin together
